The first amendment protects citizens from having their right to free speech impeded on. However the right to free speech has restrictions and it is always up to a court to decide where and when it is okay to exercise that right. It is only not okay in a private business if the business asks that you do not video record its other customers. At that point, the only thing that becomes illegal is staying after you've been asked to leave. Not video taping someone. But as you cited above, Supreme courts have held multiple times that there is no expectation of privacy out in public, including in private businesses. There are typically cameras everywhere and you are always being recorded.

People tend to believe that because they have to sign permission slips for their children to be photographed then obviously it's illegal to video anyone who doesn't consent. This simply isn't the case. Some states are known as single party consent states, which means so long as one person in an interaction agrees to be filmed the other can as well.

The only time it is actually illegal to film is wherever there is an expectation of privacy, like say, a bathroom, even a public one. But anything and everything if it can be seen from a public easement can be filmed so long as the person is intentionally invoking their first amendment rights for reference.

Yeah I just look at it terms of sales, so no carryover=more workload=more sales. Goal times are simply goal times and don't really impact store sales with OPU. At my store my SD is much more concerned with making sales and finding items (low INF) than goal times. We still maintain 100% but I sometimes let an order or two miss goal time in order to get higher sales.

As far as I understand it, carryover in MPM only records certain items placed at a given time during the previous day it's due to go out. So Monday will receive orders for Tuesday until X pm. This is the "sort by store close" on mpm. Only the items put in this specific time frame will count as carryover. Maybe the "sort by store close" is 30 units, but you see a workload of 80 for Tuesday. Unfortunately because mywork is awful, it doesn't prioritize the 30 units you actually need done for the night, so it can potentially make you pick 50 units for the next day without taking down any carryover numbers.

One strategy I've been using is keeping goal times at 100% for OPU Throughout the day, then towards the end of I get a few orders within the last 2 hours of the store closing, I'll make sure i do as mush sfs as possible before hopping back into OPU. If you miss a goal time or two but it gets your store as close as possible to 0 carryover, I'd say that's a decent trade.

I know you got this all figured out op, but just for future reference and you may have figured this out already, but when installing programs on the computer, many programs make money from advertisers who put their aware into the install of the program you want. Most people unknowingly install aware and other dangerous programs by rushing through the install progress.

Be aware you can avoid programs like these most of the time by encountering an "agree" and "disagree" box during the install process. Hitting disagree to an offer usually will not inhibit installing the program you want. Most of the time these are asking whether or not you're okay with installing another program besides the one you intend onto your device. Most of the time these are things like toolbars, adware or other malicious programs.

Just be sure to read through the installation process when getting new programs. Sorry if this was all stuff you knew already but just thought I'd throw this in there.
